what.a: An app for keeping track of your spending that doesn't feel like homework. You log what you spend, or Wambi logs it for you, and you see where your money goes each month. If you like, you set a limit per category. Wambi, a gold coin with plenty of personality, keeps you company: it cheers when you log something and gives you a heads-up when a category is filling up.

import.q: Can I bring my history from other apps?
import.a: Not yet: with end-to-end encryption, importing is on hold. Soon you'll be able to import and download your data again, now encrypted. Budge comes back first, with its CSV file; Buddy and other apps follow. Before anything is imported you'll see a preview: how many transactions come in, which ones are duplicates and which categories will be created. The file will be read on your device, and what comes in will be encrypted like everything else.

passwords.q: Why doesn't it ask for a password?
passwords.a: Because one more password wouldn't make you safer: passwords get forgotten, reused across apps and stolen. You sign in with a 6-digit code or a link sent to your email, or with a passkey: your fingerprint, your face or your phone's screen lock. A passkey is safer than a password: it can't be guessed, it never reaches our servers and it doesn't work on a fake page.

privacy.q: What do you do with my data?
privacy.a: Your data is end-to-end encrypted: it is encrypted on your device, with a key only you hold, before it leaves it. Our servers only ever receive encrypted text they can't read, except while you have an AI assistant connected: then they open what it asks for in memory, only to answer it. So we couldn't sell your data even if we wanted to: by design, we can't see it. You can delete your account whenever you want. Soon you'll be able to import and download your data again, now encrypted. The code is open source: anyone can check how it is encrypted. The details are in the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.

free.a: Yes, and it always will be. We never ask for a card.

open.a: Yes. Anyone can read Wambito's code on <github>GitHub</github>: nothing in it is hidden. It's free software, licensed under the AGPL-3.0.

meta.title: Wambito · Privacy policy
meta.description: How Wambito handles your data: what it stores, where, who can see it and how to ask us to delete it.

controller.title: Who is responsible for your data
controller.body: Wambito belongs to Slinqer S.A.S., a Colombian company. Slinqer S.A.S. is the controller of your data under Colombia's Ley 1581 de 2012 (its data protection law). This policy covers wambito.com, app.wambito.com and the Android app when it uses our server. For any question about your data, write to <email>privacy@wambito.com</email>.

data.title: What we store
data.body: Your email. Your passkeys, only their public part: the private key stays on your device. What you log or import (transactions, categories, budgets, recurring items, the category you gave each merchant, your currency) is end-to-end encrypted: it is encrypted on your device, with a key only you and your devices hold, and our server keeps it only as encrypted text it can't read. What the server does see: how many records of each kind you have, their approximate size, when they change and which are deleted; your time zone, your language and whether you finished the welcome; the platform and version of your app and the last day you opened it; the names of the devices you connect; and, if you connect an AI assistant, the permission you gave it. For each session, the kind of browser or app, never your IP address. And a minimal log of visits: when, which page and how it answered. That log keeps no IP address, nothing that comes after the “?” in addresses and no headers.

purposes.title: Why we store it
purposes.body: Your email, so you can sign in with a code or a link, and so we can answer if you write to us. Passkeys, so you can sign in without a password. Your transactions, categories, budgets and recurring items, to show you your budget: that is what the app is for, and it happens on your devices, which are the ones that hold the key. The time zone, to know when your day and your month start. The language, to speak yours, in the app and in emails. Sessions, to keep your account safe. Your IP address is used only in memory, to stop abuse such as asking for codes nonstop, and is never stored. Sign-in emails go out through an email delivery service, which only gets your address and the message.

storage.title: Where it is stored
storage.body: On a server in the European Union. Your data travels encrypted between your device and the server, and your finances stay there end-to-end encrypted. Every day we make a backup on the server and keep another copy, encrypted with age, in Cloudflare R2. No backup lasts more than 14 days: after that it deletes itself. So if you delete your account, it also leaves the backups within 14 days at most. Accounts created before end-to-end encryption moved to it on 20 November 2026; the backups from before that day still hold those finances in a form we could read, and the last of them deletes itself on 4 December 2026. One limit you should know: on the web, the app's code comes from our server every time you open it, so whoever controlled the server could change it to read your key while the page is open. The Android app doesn't have that weakness: its code is the one you installed.

analytics.title: Analytics on wambito.com
analytics.body: Only on wambito.com, and only if you accept in the cookie notice, we use PostHog to see which pages you visit and where you click, and we record the visit without what you type. PostHog Inc. is a US company that processes this data for us on its servers in the European Union, under its data processing agreement, with standard contractual clauses. It stores a random identifier in a cookie and in your browser's local storage, and records the type of browser and device. It does not keep your IP. Events are deleted after {eventsMonths, plural, one {# month} other {# months}} and recordings after {recordingsDays, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Nothing from inside the app reaches analytics: PostHog never loads on app.wambito.com or in the phone app. If your browser asks not to be tracked (GPC or Do Not Track), we don't load PostHog. You can withdraw your consent at any time in “Cookie preferences”, at the foot of every page. To have us delete what was already stored, write to <email>privacy@wambito.com</email>.

not_done.title: What we don't do
not_done.body: No trackers, no analytics, no ads. We don't sell your data or share it. It only passes through the services we need to run (the server, the backups and email delivery), and only for that.

not_done_with_analytics.title: What we don't do
not_done_with_analytics.body: No ads. We don't sell your data or share it. It only passes through the services we need to run (the server, the backups and email delivery), and only for that. On top of that, on wambito.com and only with your consent, we use PostHog to see how the page is used. Nothing from inside the app ever reaches analytics: PostHog never loads on app.wambito.com or in the phone app.

voice.title: Your voice
voice.body: In the Android app you can dictate an expense. Your voice is processed on your phone, with Vosk, and the audio never leaves it. The voice models are downloaded once, when you ask for them, from the project's releases on GitHub. Only the transaction you save leaves the phone, end-to-end encrypted, as if you had typed it.

capture.title: Automatic capture
capture.body: In the Android app you can turn on automatic capture: it starts off. If you turn it on and give Wambito access to notifications, it reads only those of the apps you choose, Revolut and Google Wallet, and ignores every other one. The notification text is processed on the phone and never leaves your phone: we neither store it nor send it. Only the transaction taken from it leaves the phone, end-to-end encrypted: the amount and currency, the merchant, the date and time, and the app it came from. It arrives marked “to review”, and you can confirm, change or delete it. To suggest the category, the app remembers the one you gave each merchant, encrypted like everything else. You can turn it off at any time in Settings → Automatic capture, or remove Wambito's access to notifications in Android's settings. On the iPhone no notification is read: if you set up in Shortcuts the Transaction automation with Wambito's “Log Wallet payment” action, Shortcuts hands Wambito the amount and currency, the merchant and the card's name of each Apple Pay payment. They are processed on the phone and only the transaction leaves it, end-to-end encrypted, as on Android; the card's name is not stored. You can turn it off in Settings → Automatic capture and delete the automation in the Shortcuts app.

assistants.title: AI assistants
assistants.body: You can connect an AI assistant to your account. It only gets in if you allow it, on a permission screen (OAuth) that tells you what it will be able to do: read your data, log things for you, or both. Since your data is end-to-end encrypted, while the assistant is connected our server opens what it asks for in memory, during each request, with a key the assistant carries, only to answer it; it never stores that key or your data unencrypted. You can take its access away whenever you like, in Settings, and it is cut at once. What the assistant reads is handled by the company that offers it, under its own policy.

guest.title: Without an email: guest mode
guest.body: In the Android app you can start without an email. Your data is stored on the server, end-to-end encrypted, in a guest account. If you add your email later, you keep it. A guest account left unused for 12 months is deleted with all its data, even if you signed out; if you protected it with a recovery key or a passkey, after 24 months.

self_hosted.title: If you use another server
self_hosted.body: Wambito's code is open source and anyone can run their own server. If your app uses a server that isn't ours, whoever runs it is the controller of your data there, not Slinqer S.A.S. This policy only covers the servers we run.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: Under Ley 1581 de 2012, you can know what data we hold about you, update it, correct it, ask us to delete it and withdraw your consent. To do so, write to <email>privacy@wambito.com</email> from your account's email. Your finances are end-to-end encrypted and we can't read them: if you ask for your data, we tell you what data we hold about you and which of it is encrypted. Without writing to us, you can <link>delete your account</link>. If you are not satisfied with our answer, you can turn to Colombia's Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If we change this policy, we publish the new version here with its date. The date at the top is that of the version in force.

meta.title: Wambito · Delete your account
meta.description: How to delete your Wambito account and the data it holds, from the app or by email.

in_app.title: From the app
in_app.body: On the web or in the Android app, go to Settings and choose “Delete my account”. To confirm, we ask you to type your email. Downloading your data first isn't possible yet: soon you'll be able to import and download your data again, now encrypted. If you use the app as a guest, save your progress with an email first; otherwise your account deletes itself after 12 months unused.

by_email.title: By email
by_email.body: If you can't sign in, write to <email>privacy@wambito.com</email> from your account's email and ask us to delete it. We'll let you know when it's done.

what_goes.title: What is deleted
what_goes.body: Everything in your account, right away: your account, your email, your passkeys and sessions, your transactions, categories, budgets and recurring items, and the permissions of the assistants you connected. On the phone, the app also clears what it kept of your account.

backups.title: Backups
backups.body: Backups that include your account delete themselves within 14 days at most. The copy that leaves the server is encrypted. There are more details in the <link>privacy policy</link>.
